question: Which is a beta-emitting radioactive isotope of hydrogen that has one proton and two neutrons in its nucleus, making it three times as heavy as a hydrogen nucleus and one and a half times heavier than deuterium?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tritium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tritium

 
 
• It is a beta-emitting radioactive isotope of hydrogen.
 
• Its nucleus consists of one proton and two neutrons, making it three times as heavy as a hydrogen nucleus (with its one proton) and one-and-a-half times as heavy as deuterium (which contains one proton and only one neutron).
 
• Tritium would no longer exist in our environment if cosmic radiation produces it in the atmosphere in very small amounts.
 
• The half-life of the unstable tritium nucleus is of 12.3 years, which is very short on the radioactive time scale.
 
 
• This comparatively fast disappearance means that very little tritium can accumulate in any place.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Protium
 
 
 
• **Protium **has no neutrons in its nucleus.
 
• It is considered the most stable isotope of hydrogen.
 
• The basic hydrogen atom – a single proton circled by a single electron is also called protium.
 
 
 
 

 Hydrogen-4
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen-4** is a **highly unstable isotope of hydrogen.**
 
• The nucleus consists of **a proton** and **three neutrons**.
